meta.title: Business Diagnostic — Know where your business stands
meta.description: The Forcelis Business Diagnostic analyzes financial and operational information to identify risks, inefficiencies and opportunities, and delivers a Forcelis Business Score with recommended actions.

hero.title: Know where your business stands.
hero.subtitle: A structured analysis of your financial and operational information that identifies risks, inefficiencies and opportunities for improvement — and states what to do about each one.

score.title: Forcelis Business Score
score.intro: Five dimensions, scored on the same scale so they can be compared against each other and against the same company a period later. The score is not the deliverable — it is the index into it.

items.label: Financial health
items.note: Margin structure, cost base and result quality

items.label: Cash flow
items.note: Real collection, aging and cash conversion

items.label: Commercial performance
items.note: Customer mix, concentration, retention and pricing

items.label: Accounting data quality
items.note: Completeness and consistency of the underlying records

score.footnote: Scores shown are illustrative and do not describe any real company.

analysis.title: What gets analyzed
analysis.intro: Four areas, read together. Most of the findings that matter live at the seams between them.

findings.title: Findings, stated as decisions.
findings.intro: Each finding names what was observed, why it matters, and what should be done. The examples below are illustrative.

items.title: Customer concentration represents a material commercial risk.
items.body: The top five customers account for a share of revenue at which the loss of one materially changes the year.
items.action: Quantify the exposure per customer and set a concentration target for the next four quarters.

items.title: Accounts receivable grew faster than revenue.
items.body: Collection is slowing relative to sales. The gap is financed by the company, and it does not show up in the income statement.
items.action: Review credit terms by customer segment and separate genuine disputes from routine late payment.

items.title: Inventory turnover is below expected performance.
items.body: A share of working capital is held in items that are not moving at the rate the rest of the catalogue does.
items.action: Identify the slow-moving items by value and decide, per item, whether to discount, return or stop reordering.

items.title: Gross margin decreased in a key product category.
items.body: The decline is driven by input cost, not by price. It has been absorbed rather than passed through.
items.action: Compare purchase price movement against list price by category and decide where to reprice.

deliverables.title: A document your management team can work from.

items.title: Executive summary
items.body: The situation in one page, written for someone who will not read the rest.

items.title: Financial analysis
items.body: Results, margins, costs and cash, restated in managerial terms with history.

items.title: Operational analysis
items.body: Inventory, purchasing, suppliers and the working capital they consume.

items.title: Key risks
items.body: What could damage the business, ordered by exposure rather than by ease of fixing.

items.title: Key opportunities
items.body: Where margin, cash or capacity is recoverable, with an estimated size.

items.title: Recommended actions
items.body: A short, sequenced list with an owner and a way to measure each one.

process.title: Four steps, no system access required.

steps.title: Scope conversation
steps.body: A short call to understand the business, the period to analyze and the questions management already has.

steps.title: You send the information
steps.body: Files you download from your own systems. Forcelis never asks for your tax portal or banking credentials.

steps.title: Analysis
steps.body: Ingestion, normalization and analysis on the platform, followed by review by the people who will present it.

steps.title: Findings session
steps.body: A working session on the results and the recommended actions, with the full document delivered afterwards.

inputs.title: What is needed from you
inputs.intro: The minimum is the first item. Everything else improves the depth of the analysis but is not required to start.
items: CFDI for the period — issued and received, including payment complements
Trial balance or general ledger, if available
Inventory report, if the business holds stock
Sales detail by customer and product, if it is kept outside invoicing
inputs.note: If something is missing, the affected metric is reported as unavailable with the reason. It is not estimated.

closing.title: Start with the diagnostic.
closing.body: It establishes the baseline. Everything after it — advisory, platform, managed services — is scoped from evidence rather than from a proposal.
